title: Edge cases for dates and time zones
when: A feature handles dates, times, schedules, deadlines or ages, and the user wants it tested for date and time zone bugs.
inputs: where dates are created, stored and shown
prompt:
Goal: A check of date logic across zones, daylight saving shifts, month ends and formats, with exact failing inputs.
Steps:
1. Find where dates are made and parsed (new Date(string), Date.parse, date inputs, stored timestamps) and whether each is local or UTC.
2. Parsing: "2026-03-08" is read as UTC midnight but "2026-03-08T00:00" as local; show a date only value in a UTC-3 zone to expose the day off bug.
3. Daylight saving: adding 24 hours across a shift is not adding one calendar day; 23 and 25 hour days must not skip or repeat dates.
4. Calendar: Jan 31 plus one month, Feb 29 in leap and common years, Dec 31 to Jan 1, weeks starting Sunday or Monday.
5. Display: Intl.DateTimeFormat with the user locale and an explicit timeZone; 12 and 24 hour clocks; relative times near midnight.
6. Vary the zone per run: TZ=America/Sao_Paulo node --test, then TZ=Asia/Kolkata for a half hour offset.
Quality bar:
- Each bug shows zone, input and wrong output.
- Storage format proposed: ISO 8601 in UTC or with offset.
- Tests use fixed dates, never today.
Pitfalls:
- Testing only in your own zone.
- Using the current date as test data.
- Assuming every day has 24 hours.
Verify:
- [ ] Parse sites listed.
- [ ] DST and month end cases run.
- [ ] Two or more zones tested.
- [ ] Findings have exact inputs.
Output: date-edge-cases.md with findings, and test/dates.test.mjs if tests were added.

examples.input: the due date shows one day early for some users
examples.output: new Date("2026-05-10") is UTC, shown in UTC-3 as May 9; fix: parse as local parts or store with offset
